newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks end mixed as supermarket dives.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks end mixed as supermarket dives.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in busy sessions that saw supermarket chain Cadenalco take a dive, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB index edged up 0.03 percent to 841.52 amid a two billion peso trade, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.63 percent to 13,247.45 in trading also worth about two billion pesos.

"An investor desperate for liquidity went on a selling spree and jettisonned Cadenalco shares regardless of whether there was any demand for them or not. He sold them very cheap," a Bogota broker said.

Cadenalco crashed 5.76 percent to 801, its lowest price of the year, in a 449 million peso trade on the Bogota exchange. In Medellin, the supermarket chain, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, plunged 9.6 percent to 800 in a 488 million peso trade.
The chain's third quarter profits dropped on the back of a sector that was stagnant in the second quarter and grew just 0.5 percent in the third quarter.
"We don't know of any other significant reasons why Cadenalco is falling. Some shareholders are even asking to sell futures another dealer said.
At this time last year, Cadenalco shares stood at 1,300 pesos each.
The Bogota index was, however, driven up by demand for brewing giant Bavaria, which rose 1.58 percent to 4,099 in a 366.5 million peso volume.
"We're recommending buys in Bavaria because of solid long- term prospects. It's an easy-to-sell share that is good for speculating with or investing in," one dealer said.
On the Medellin exchange, Bavaria rose 0.62 percent to 4,055 in a 453 million peso volume.
